title: Best Session Singers and Vocalists (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a session singer online: what the package should include, what to send, file formats, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: Session singers record vocals for your song from their own studio: lead vocals, harmonies or backing parts. Remote recording works well when the singer receives a clear guide and the rights are agreed upfront. It goes wrong when the key is wrong, files arrive in the wrong format, or the singer later claims a share of the song. This guide helps you get vocals ready for mixing.

faq.q: What should I send the singer?
faq.a: An instrumental track, lyrics, a guide melody or rough vocal, the tempo and key, and reference songs for the vocal style.
Usually dry vocal tracks, without effects, as WAV files, plus a rough mix. Ask for separate tracks for lead, harmonies and doubles.
Sometimes. Some singers deliver raw takes; others edit and tune them. Clarify this, and read our mixing guide for the next step.
Agree in writing. Many session singers work for a fee with no royalties; others ask for a credit or share. Settle it before recording.

faq.q: What if the key does not suit the singer?
faq.a: Share the instrumental early and ask the singer to confirm the key fits their range before recording starts.
